hero.purpose: The product's opening claim. Once per surface, text-wrap balanced.

figure.purpose: A single headline number: a total, a saving, a percentage. Always tabular.

title.purpose: The name of a thing in a list — an item, a product, a person.

value.purpose: A fact's value beside its label. Tabular.

label.purpose: Uppercase state words, actor tags and eyebrows.

caption.purpose: Figure labels and secondary notes, in ink-faint.

mono.purpose: Identifiers only — run ids, pool ids, digests, ARNs. Never a price.

shadows.name: shadow-sm
shadows.purpose: A panel at rest. The default, and usually the only shadow on screen. Dark theme: 0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,0.4).

shadows.name: shadow-md
shadows.purpose: Hover on the primary action, and small floating surfaces. Dark theme re-tunes to pure black at 0.6/0.4.

shadows.name: shadow-lg
shadows.purpose: Drawers and overlays only. Dark theme re-tunes to pure black at 0.8/0.4.

motion.name: ease-expo-out
motion.purpose: The only easing in the system. Every transform, entrance and meter fill uses it.

motion.name: duration-state
motion.purpose: Standard state change: background, colour, border on hover and selection.

motion.name: duration-press
motion.purpose: Active press displacement on a button (translateY 1px).

motion.name: duration-fade
motion.purpose: Opacity-only appearance of a small overlay.

motion.name: duration-enter
motion.purpose: Slide-in of a drawer or panel that genuinely arrived.

motion.name: duration-reveal
motion.purpose: Reveal of a narrative block. Legitimate in Showcase; not on consumer surfaces.

motion.name: duration-meter
motion.purpose: A meter filling via scaleX. The longest motion in the system, because it is the one carrying arithmetic.

motion.name: pulse-live
motion.purpose: The single continuous animation. Marks a genuinely live connection and nothing else.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Global kill under prefers-reduced-motion, plus scroll-behavior auto. Information must survive it.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one action a screen wants. Ink on paper, never a brand hue and never an actor hue — the semantic colours are spoken for by attribution.
components.html: <button class="ds-btn ds-btn-primary">Ask Pool to check now</button>
components.css: .ds-btn { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; padding: 9px 15px; border-radius: 8px; border: 1px solid var(--rule-strong, #c6bdab); background: var(--paper-raised, #fffdfa); color: var(--ink, #17150f); font-family: inherit; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 550; cursor: pointer; transition: background 130ms ease, border-color 130ms ease, transform 80ms ease, box-shadow 130ms ease; } .ds-btn-primary { background: var(--ink, #17150f); border-color: var(--ink, #17150f); color: var(--paper, #f7f4ef); box-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgba(23,21,15,0.05); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--ink, #17150f) 88%, #000); border-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--ink, #17150f) 88%, #000); box-shadow: 0 4px 14px -6px rgba(23,21,15,0.18), 0 1px 3px rgba(23,21,15,0.05); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: translateY(1px); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--ink, #17150f); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: The ordinary control. A real edge on raised paper — quiet, but not a ghost.
components.css: .ds-btn2 { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; padding: 9px 15px; border-radius: 8px; border: 1px solid var(--rule-strong, #c6bdab); background: var(--paper-raised, #fffdfa); color: var(--ink, #17150f); font-family: inherit; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 550; cursor: pointer; transition: background 130ms ease, border-color 130ms ease, transform 80ms ease; } .ds-btn2:hover { background: var(--paper-sunken, #efeae1); border-color: var(--ink-faint, #6f6759); } .ds-btn2:active { transform: translateY(1px); } .ds-btn2:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--ink, #17150f); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Accept Button
components.description: The affirmative control a person presses. Clay because a human is the actor — not moss, which would attribute the decision to the agent.
components.css: .ds-btn-accept { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; padding: 9px 15px; border-radius: 8px; border: 1px solid var(--clay, #a0512a); background: var(--clay, #a0512a); color: var(--paper-raised, #fffdfa); font-family: inherit; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 550; cursor: pointer; transition: background 130ms ease, transform 80ms ease; } .ds-btn-accept:hover { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--clay, #a0512a) 88%, #000); } .ds-btn-accept:active { transform: translateY(1px); } .ds-btn-accept:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--ink, #17150f); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: 38px minimum height is functional, not aesthetic: iOS zooms the page when focused text is under 16px.
components.html: <input class="ds-input" type="text" placeholder="What do you buy?" />
components.css: .ds-input { width: 100%; box-sizing: border-box; padding: 9px 11px; min-height: 38px; border-radius: 8px; border: 1px solid var(--rule-strong, #c6bdab); background: var(--paper-raised, #fffdfa); color: var(--ink, #17150f); font-family: inherit; font-size: 14px; transition: border-color 130ms ease; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: var(--ink-faint, #6f6759); } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--ink, #17150f); outline-offset: 1px; border-color: var(--ink, #17150f); }

components.name: Panel
components.description: Raised paper inside a hairline rule, at a 14px radius. Clips its children so a full-bleed child cannot square the corner.
components.html:
Jasmine rice, 5 lb

7 people near you buy this — 24 bags standing, 2 of them yours.
components.css: .ds-panel { background: var(--paper-raised, #fffdfa); border: 1px solid var(--rule, #ded7c9); border-radius: 14px; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgba(23,21,15,0.05); overflow: hidden; } .ds-panel-body { padding: 16px 18px; } .ds-panel-title { margin: 0; font-family: 'Instrument Serif', 'Iowan Old Style', Georgia, serif; font-weight: 400; font-size: 19px; line-height: 1.2; color: var(--ink, #17150f); } .ds-panel-note { margin: 6px 0 0; font-size: 14px; line-height: 1.55; color: var(--ink-muted, #575145); }

components.name: Navigation
components.description: Text buttons; the current page is a solid ink pill rather than an underline, so it survives a horizontally scrolling rail on a phone.
components.html: <nav class="ds-nav"><button class="ds-nav-item" aria-current="page">Home</button><button class="ds-nav-item">Orders</button><button class="ds-nav-item">What you buy</button></nav>
components.css: .ds-nav { display: flex; gap: 2px; align-items: center; } .ds-nav-item { background: none; border: none; cursor: pointer; min-height: 30px; padding: 6px 11px; border-radius: 7px; color: var(--ink-muted, #575145); font-family: inherit; font-size: 13.5px; font-weight: 500; white-space: nowrap; transition: background 130ms ease, color 130ms ease; } .ds-nav-item:hover { background: var(--paper-sunken, #efeae1); color: var(--ink, #17150f); } .ds-nav-item[aria-current='page'] { background: var(--ink, #17150f); color: var(--paper, #f7f4ef); } .ds-nav-item:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--ink, #17150f); outline-offset: -2px; }

components.name: Chip
components.description: A pill for a small qualifier. The live variant’s pulsing dot is the system’s only continuous animation and marks a genuinely live connection; it stays ink, because a live runtime is neither a person nor a decision.
components.css: .ds-chip { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 5px; padding: 2px 8px; border-radius: 999px; border: 1px solid var(--rule-strong, #c6bdab); background: var(--paper-sunken, #efeae1); color: var(--ink-muted, #575145); font-family: inherit; font-size: 11.5px; font-weight: 600; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-chip-live { color: var(--ink, #17150f); border-color: var(--rule-strong, #c6bdab); background: var(--paper-sunken, #efeae1); } .ds-chip-live::before { content: ''; width: 6px; height: 6px; border-radius: 50%; background: currentColor; animation: ds-pulse 2s ease-in-out infinite; } @keyframes ds-pulse { 0%, 100% { opacity: 1; } 50% { opacity: 0.35; } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-chip-live::before { animation-duration: 0.01ms; } }

components.name: Attribution Tag
components.description: The signature component. Every action is attributable to exactly one of three parties, and the whole technical argument of the project is which. Hue plus shape, so it survives greyscale and video re-encoding.
components.html: Agent decidedComputedPerson asked
components.css: .ds-actors { display: flex; gap: 18px; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: center; } .ds-actor { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 7px; font-family: inherit; font-size: 11.5px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.04em; text-transform: uppercase; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-actor-glyph { width: 9px; height: 9px; flex: none; } .ds-actor-agent { color: var(--moss, #3d6b4c); } .ds-actor-engine { color: var(--graphite, #384b5e); } .ds-actor-human { color: var(--clay, #a0512a); }

components.name: Consumer State Chip
components.description: One of exactly five state words with its deterministic reason underneath. Clay only on "needs you", where a person must act; the other four are neutral, because "the system is working" is not one party. Below 560px it becomes a line under the name instead of a column beside it.
components.css: .ds-status { display: inline-flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: flex-end; text-align: right; gap: 1px; min-width: 0; } .ds-status-word { font-family: inherit; font-size: 11.5px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.05em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--ink-faint, #6f6759); } .ds-status-reason { font-family: inherit; font-size: 12.5px; color: var(--ink-muted, #575145); } .ds-status.is-needs-you .ds-status-word { color: var(--clay, #a0512a); } .ds-status.is-coordinating .ds-status-word, .ds-status.is-ready .ds-status-word, .ds-status.is-done .ds-status-word { color: var(--ink, #17150f); } @media (max-width: 560px) { .ds-status { align-items: flex-start; text-align: left; } }

components.name: Meter
components.description: A 6px pill carrying arithmetic. Ink fill, dropping to ink-muted when short of a threshold: a meter reports magnitude, not who acted, so it takes no actor hue. Animated with scaleX rather than width, because a width transition is a layout animation and these sit inside lists that are still settling.
components.css: .ds-meter { position: relative; height: 6px; border-radius: 999px; background: var(--paper-deep, #e7e1d5); overflow: hidden; } .ds-meter-fill { height: 100%; width: 100%; background: var(--ink, #17150f); border-radius: 999px; transform-origin: left center; transition: transform 600ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .ds-meter-fill.is-short { background: var(--ink-muted, #575145); } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-meter-fill { transition-duration: 0.01ms; } }

components.name: Case-Fit Diagram
components.description: Signature. Replaces three sentences of case-fitting arithmetic with a picture in which the no-speculative-surplus invariant is visible at a glance. Solid box = a whole case Pool bought; dashed box = the remainder it did not, because a solid box around a partial case would imply a purchase that never happened. The reader’s own units are ink rather than an actor hue: ownership is emphasis, not attribution.
components.html:
12 / 12 filled
still on your list
components.css: .ds-casefit { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 8px; } .ds-casefit-row { display: flex; align-items: center; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 8px; } .ds-casefit-case { display: inline-flex; gap: 2px; padding: 3px; border: 1px solid var(--rule-strong, #c6bdab); border-radius: 4px; background: var(--paper-sunken, #efeae1); } .ds-casefit-case.is-left { border-style: dashed; background: transparent; } .ds-unit { width: 9px; height: 15px; border-radius: 2px; background: var(--rule-strong, #c6bdab); } .ds-unit.is-mine { background: var(--ink, #17150f); } .ds-unit.is-standing { background: transparent; border: 1px dashed var(--rule-strong, #c6bdab); } .ds-casefit-total, .ds-casefit-note { font-family: inherit; font-size: 12px; color: var(--ink-muted, #575145); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }

narrative.overview:
Pool looks like a ledger somebody keeps by hand and can hand to an auditor. Warm paper (#f7f4ef), dark ink, hairline rules doing the structural work, figures set in tabular numerals so columns of money line up, and a serif display face for the numbers and names that matter. A ledger's authority does not come from decoration; it comes from being inspectable line by line. That is exactly the claim this product makes about an autonomous agent, so the interface makes the claim in its own material rather than asserting it in copy.

The density is low and the surfaces are quiet. Colour is scarce and strictly semantic: three hues that mean who was responsible — moss for the agent, graphite for deterministic code, clay for a person — and one red that means something broke. Nothing else gets to be coloured. Success, ownership, progress and magnitude are all neutral, and when a screen has no attribution to make, it is paper, ink, and rule. The reward for that restraint is that the moment colour appears, it means something, and a viewer learns the grammar in one screen without a legend.

The system is deliberately unlike four neighbours. It is not an operations console, not AI product chrome, not a consumer savings app, and not an enterprise procurement tool. The first is a lived failure rather than a taste: an earlier build put the same information on screen three times in dense counter grids, and a correct system read as an admin dashboard.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper and ink; four paper tones carry depth instead of shadow.
Instrument Serif for names, headlines and figures; system sans for everything read in sentences; monospace only for identifiers.
Colour is attribution, never emphasis. Three semantic hues, one failure red, and no fourth accent. Success, ownership and magnitude are neutral.
Tabular numerals wherever a number could be compared to another number.
Hairline rules (1px) as the primary structural device.
Full dark mode, token-for-token, at the same semantic meanings.
Attribution is redundantly encoded as shape — diamond, square, circle — so it survives greyscale, colour-blindness and video re-encoding.

rules.name: The Attribution Rule
rules.body: The three hues mean who was responsible and nothing else. Moss is the agent, graphite is deterministic code, clay is a human. They are never spent on hierarchy, emphasis, decoration, mood, success, ownership or magnitude, and no fourth accent may be introduced. A new colour may only be a tone inside an existing role. Colour is the cheapest proof the interface has of the product's central claim; spending it on emphasis destroys the proof.

rules.name: The Neutral-Unless-Attributed Rule
rules.body: If a mark does not name which party acted, it is neutral. Progress, totals, completion, ownership and chrome are ink, ink-muted, ink-faint or a paper tone, distinguished by tone, weight and type rather than hue. When such a mark does need attribution, add the attribution tag beside it — never tint the mark itself.

rules.name: The Stop Means Broken Rule
rules.body: `stop` says a thing failed: a card declined, a row rejected, a run that did not complete. It never says no. Pool declining to coordinate is a computed result and renders in the neutral field with its reason attached.

rules.name: The Colour Is Never Alone Rule
rules.body: Every state distinguished by colour is also distinguished by a word, and attribution is also distinguished by shape. A state must be readable in greyscale, because the demo is watched as re-encoded video.

rules.name: The Serif Means Consequence Rule
rules.body: Instrument Serif is reserved for names, headlines and figures. It never sets prose, never sets a label, and never sets a control. If it appears, the thing it sets is one a reader is meant to remember.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Any number a reader could compare to another number is font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums. Money, units, counts, percentages, elapsed time. Non-negotiable: a ledger whose columns do not align is not a ledger.

rules.name: The Mono Is For Machines Rule
rules.body: Monospace marks a value a human is meant to copy or verify, not a value a human is meant to understand. Identifiers, digests, hashes. A price is never mono.

rules.name: The One Frame Rule
rules.body: On a demo-critical screen, the thing that changed and the reason it changed are visible together without scrolling. A scroll that falls between a number and the sentence explaining it is a defect.

rules.name: The Never Zoom Out Rule
rules.body: Density is solved by removing repetition, never by shrinking type or asking the viewer to zoom. Everything is designed at 100% zoom at 1280x720, 1440x900 and 390x844.

rules.name: The Shadow Earns Its Place Rule
rules.body: A shadow means this is above the page or this responded to you. It never means this is important. Importance is tone, rule and type.

rules.name: The Dashed Outline Rule
rules.body: Dashed edges mean unbought, unfilled, or still standing. Never use a dashed border for style.

dos: Do encode attribution with both hue and shape, and let the legend appear once.
Do keep the focus ring ink, and keep generic chrome neutral. An actor hue on a focus ring, a banner or a heading attributes an action that nothing performed.
Do reach for ink, ink-muted or a paper tone for success, completion, ownership and progress, and add an attribution tag when the actor genuinely matters.
Do set every comparable number in tabular numerals.
Do reach for a paper tone and a 1px rule before reaching for a shadow.
Do keep Instrument Serif for names, headlines and figures only.
Do animate transform and opacity. The one easing is cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); state changes are 0.13s, entrances 0.28–0.42s, and the meter is 0.6s.

Do let motion report a change that actually happened. On consumer surfaces an element may animate only when its own state changed — nothing on first paint, nothing on scroll. Showcase is a narrative reader, so sequenced reveal of already-computed facts is legitimate there.
Do honour prefers-reduced-motion, and make sure the information survives with motion off. Motion explains a change; it is never the only thing carrying it.
Do draw the arithmetic when a diagram replaces a paragraph — cases, thresholds, distances, recoveries.
Do give a refusal the same typographic dignity as a success.
Do keep contrast at WCAG 2.2 AA, and keep small text at ink-faint or darker.
donts: Don't spend moss, graphite or clay on emphasis, hierarchy, mood, success, ownership or magnitude, and don't add a fourth accent. Colour is attribution.
Don't use moss as a success or done colour. Moss means the agent decided something; a green tick on a step nobody chose is a false claim about who acted.
Don't use graphite for the focus ring or for generic chrome. Generic focus is ink.
Don't use stop red for Pool declining to coordinate. That is a correct answer, not an error. Stop is for a thing that broke.

Don't animate anything that implies work in progress the system is not doing — no fabricated thinking, no fake tool progress, no spinner on a step the browser cannot observe. A pulsing dot means a live connection; nothing else may borrow it.
Don't dim a disabled control to a 45% ghost. Flatten it and keep the label legible.
Don't animate width, height, top or left.
Don't solve density by shrinking type or expecting a zoom-out.
Don't put a dashed border on anything that is not literally unbought or unfilled.
Don't set a price, a total or a name in monospace. Mono is for identifiers.
Don't let this become an operations console: no dense counter grids, no metric walls, no sidebar-and-table chrome, and never the same fact in three sections of one screen.
Don't let this become AI product chrome: no purple-blue gradients, no sparkle or wand iconography, no glowing thinking state, no typewriter text.
Don't let this become a consumer savings app: no confetti on a saving, no trophy percentage, no cartoon illustration, no mint-and-white rounded card deck.
Don't let this become an enterprise procurement tool: no grey-on-grey field walls, no tabbed record view standing in for hierarchy.
Don't use emoji. Icons are one stroke weight on one grid, inline SVG.
